answers.question: Global temperature outcome by 2100
answers.answer: Three temperature outcomes are described: 1.5°C (Net-Zero 2050, aligned with NGFS Net Zero 2050 at 1.5°C); below 2°C (Delayed Transition, aligned with NGFS Delayed Transition at 1.8°C); and greater than 3°C (Current Policies/Hothouse, aligned with NGFS Current Policies at >3°C). The Delayed Transition scenario involves a temporary overshoot of the carbon budget before declining. The Current Policies scenario leads to 3°C of warming with emissions growing until 2080.
answers.evidence: "NGFS Net Zero 2050 (1.5°C) | NGFS Delayed Transition (1.8°C) | NGFS Current Policies (>3°C)" and "This scenario assumes the continuation of any currently implemented climate policies and no further action. There is slow technology uptake and low CO2 removal, with emissions growing until 2080 leading to 3°C of warming and severe physical risks." and "emissions exceed the carbon budget temporarily and subsequently decline faster than in other scenarios."
answers.notes: Temperature overshoot is explicitly mentioned for the Delayed Transition scenario.
